# llms.txt: AI-friendly guide to the insurer search repo

This file helps LLMs understand the key docs and entry points.

## Overview

A typo-tolerant search for US health insurers (payers) on Databricks Lakebase. One REST endpoint, service-principal OAuth, no client-side database connection. Built for an EHR's insurance company dropdown.

## Key files to read

### Documentation
- **[README.md](README.md)** — Start here. What it does, how it works, quick start, performance numbers.
- **[docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md)** — How it works under the hood (Postgres, Lakebase, GiST + BM25).
- **[docs/search-quality.md](docs/search-quality.md)** — Synonyms, exact-name matching, and quality metrics (98.4% brand@10, v2).
- **[docs/operations.md](docs/operations.md)** — Refresh (zero downtime), CU sizing (2–32 CU), cold start, monitoring.
- **[docs/security.md](docs/security.md)** — OAuth, audit log, HIPAA compliance, Private Link.

- **[sql/20_search_function.sql](sql/20_search_function.sql)** — Search function (trigram + BM25, "did you mean", scoring).

### Results & evidence
- **[results/exact-name-deepdive-2026-10-06.md](results/exact-name-deepdive-2026-10-06.md)** — v2 load test: 315–331 rps at 16 CU. Why 100 candidates + full BM25 scoring = 0 misses. 98.4% brand@10.
- **[results/quality-fn-v2-synfix.json](results/quality-fn-v2-synfix.json)** — v2 evaluator (899 queries, 98.4% brand@10, 0 exact-name misses).
- **[results/loadtest-2026-10-06.md](results/loadtest-2026-10-06.md)** — v1: 200–245 rps at 16 CU (original function for reference).
- **[results/loadtest-cu32-2026-10-06.md](results/loadtest-cu32-2026-10-06.md)** — v1: 32 CU: 440–465 rps (single-endpoint max). 1 CU OOM warning.
- **[results/coldstart-2026-10-06.md](results/coldstart-2026-10-06.md)** — Cold start: 1.6 s (not an error), then ~140 ms.
- **[results/zero-downtime-2026-10-06.md](results/zero-downtime-2026-10-06.md)** — 7,486/7,486 searches succeeded during full sync + index refresh.

## Quick reference

### How it works
1. **Sync**: Unity Catalog Delta table → Lakebase SNAPSHOT synced table (3M rows).
2. **Index**: 3M rows → 33k normalized search keys (Materialized View).
3. **Search**: Query → trigram KNN (100 keys) + BM25 (100 keys) + unified scoring.
4. **Result**: Ranked payers (best first), 10 per page, 50 max.
5. **Audit**: One row per search (query, tenant, caller, duration).

### Performance (AWS, 3M rows, v2)
- **Throughput**: ~315–331 requests/s at 16 CU (v2). 32 CU max: ~440–465 rps (v1 for reference).
- **Latency**: p50 ~27–64 ms (10–25 users). p50 9.8 ms inside Postgres (exact-name sweep).
- **Bottleneck**: Database CPU.

### Search quality (v2)
- **Brand@10**: 98.4% (899 generated queries, [quality-fn-v2-synfix.json](results/quality-fn-v2-synfix.json)).
- **Exact-name misses**: 0 / 6,291 payers. Wider-word queries: 80 / 88 in the top 10 ([results/wider-word-2026-10-07.md](results/wider-word-2026-10-07.md)).
- **Per-kind**: exact 99.3%, typo 98.0%, brand_typo 99.3%, joined 100%, state_first 100%, initials 98.9%, dropped 91.1%.

### Security
- **Auth**: Service-principal OAuth (M2M, 1 h expiry).
- **Data access**: One function, `SECURITY DEFINER` owned by a `NOLOGIN` role.
- **Audit**: Per-search log (query, tenant, caller, duration).
- **Compliance**: HIPAA supported, pgaudit included, Private Link available.

## Common tasks

| Task | Files |
|---|---|
| **Deploy** | `scripts/setup.sh` (idempotent) |
| **Refresh data** | `SKIP_DATA=1 scripts/setup.sh` |
| **Add synonyms** | Edit `data/seed/synonyms.csv`, then `SKIP_DATA=1 scripts/setup.sh` |
| **Test quality** | `uv run python -m insurer_search.evaluate --sample 150` |
| **Load test** | `uv run python scripts/run_loadtest.py --tasks 4 --steps 10,25,50,100,200,400` |
| **Run tests** | `uv run pytest` (offline + live suite) |
| **Call API** | See [README: Call it](README.md#call-it) for curl/Python examples |

- **1 CU returns HTTP 500 out of memory** at 200+ users ([results/loadtest-cu32-2026-10-06.md](results/loadtest-cu32-2026-10-06.md), failed earlier attempt)

## Decision records

- **[ADR 0001](docs/adr/0001-lakebase-data-api-not-model-serving.md)**: Why Data API (REST) not Model Serving (gRPC).
- **[ADR 0002](docs/adr/0002-trigram-plus-bm25.md)**: Why both trigram (typo tolerance) and BM25 (synonyms, multi-word).
- **[ADR 0003](docs/adr/0003-search-normalised-keys-not-raw-aliases.md)**: Why normalize & deduplicate upfront (scale follows corpus, not alias count).
- **[ADR 0004](docs/adr/0004-definer-function-is-the-only-door.md)**: Why SECURITY DEFINER (the function owns all data access, no client access to tables).

```
├── scripts/

│   ├── run_loadtest.py    # Load test runner (Locust in-region)
│   ├── zero_downtime_check.py # Zero-downtime verification
│   └── ops/               # Operational tools (refresh, CU change, etc.)

│   ├── locustfile.py      # Locust load script

│   └── synonyms_generated.csv # Generated by synonyms.py (initials, etc.)
└── results/               # Measurement results (load test, cold start, quality)
```

## Questions an LLM might ask

1. **How does the system ensure a brand name is not erased by a hypernym synonym?**
   See [Search quality: Synonym rules](docs/search-quality.md#synonym-rules-replace-vs-expand). The rule checks if a word is a live brand in the payer list; if so, it expands instead of replacing.

2. **Why is the exact-name miss rate zero while the load test shows 0 failures but not 0 latency variance?**
   Exact-name miss rate is a quality metric (does the payer appear in top 50). Latency variance is a performance metric (how spread out is response time). Both are measured, both are 0 failures / low variance respectively ([sources](results/)).

3. **How do I know when to increase CU?**
   Watch `audit.search_log.duration_ms` (in-database time) and client-side latency. If p50 latency > 100 ms or p99 > 500 ms, increase CU (measured ceiling at each level in [load tests](results/loadtest-2026-10-06.md)).

4. **What is the difference between a SNAPSHOT and a TRIGGERED sync?**
   SNAPSHOT copies the entire table once (idempotent, ~60 s for 3M rows). TRIGGERED copies only changes (CDC, requires source table to have CDF). The search uses SNAPSHOT (simpler, no ongoing CDC cost).

5. **Can I run this on Azure?**
   Yes, the API is the same. Load tests were on AWS. To verify on Azure, run your own load test (same code, point at Azure endpoint).
